title: Lindblad theory of linear response susceptibility and dispersive readout in minimal Kitaev junctions
authors: Tobias Kuhn, Raffael L. Klees, Ramón Aguado, Mónica Benito
abstract: The field of hybrid superconductor-semiconductor quantum dots is advancing toward the development of functional devices that leverage the advantages of both types of materials. However, the inherent complexity of these devices demands a comprehensive theoretical framework for a complete understanding of their responses to external probes, readout and the dissipation arising from environmental coupling. We present a Lindblad-based linear response formalism that captures the multi-level nature of these devices, their probe-readout flexibility, and the non-unitary effects of finite-frequency response, including the so-called Sisyphus and Hermes dynamical susceptibilities. These arise from fluctuations in the rates and jump operators, and are hence absent in standard Kubo linear response treatments. We exemplify the framework using quantum dot-based Kitaev chain setups which are promising candidates for topologically protected Majorana-based parity qubits. Our results shed light onto the validity of the standard curvature-based approximation for fermionic parity and qubit readout, show that Hermes terms compensate decoherence in dispersive readout and implement important corrections beyond thermalized states.
summary: The paper introduces a novel Lindblad-based linear response formalism to analyze complex superconducting quantum dot devices. It extends beyond standard Kubo treatments by incorporating Sisyphus and Hermes susceptibilities, which account for finite-frequency, non-unitary environmental effects. This framework is vital for accurately modeling qubit readout in topological systems like Kitaev junctions.
main_problem: Developing a comprehensive theoretical framework to understand the response of hybrid superconductor-semiconductor quantum dots (SCQDs) to external probes, including readout and environmental dissipation.
main_result: The formalism successfully captures Sisyphus and Hermes dynamical susceptibilities, which are non-unitary effects absent in standard Kubo treatments, showing that Hermes terms can compensate decoherence in dispersive readout.
method: A Lindblad-based linear response formalism is employed to calculate the total susceptibility by decomposing it into four contributions ($\chi_{st}, \chi_H, \chi_\Gamma, \chi_L$).
model_or_system: The study uses minimal Kitaev junctions (MKCs) hosting topologically protected Majorana-based parity qubits within hybrid SCQD devices.
key_observables: Linear response susceptibility $\chi(\omega)$, Quantum Capacitance ($	ext{CQ}$), and the distinct Sisyphus ($\chi_\Gamma$) and Hermes ($\chi_L$) susceptibilities.
important_parameters: The energy gap ($\epsilon$), onsite potentials ($\mu$), and coupling strengths ($\Delta, t$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include Born-Markov approximations (weakly coupled environment) and assuming a time-independent reference state $ho$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the decomposition of susceptibility contributions ($\chi_{st}, \chi_H, \chi_\Gamma, \chi_L$) in various coupling regimes, comparing theoretical predictions to band curvature estimates.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the Lindblad formalism for response theory, details the calculation and physical origin of Sisyphus and Hermes terms, applies this framework to Kitaev junctions, and analyzes specific measurements like dispersive readout and common gate spectroscopy.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced tools for analyzing open quantum systems relevant to solid-state qubits, extending standard linear response theory to account for non-unitary dissipation effects crucial for accurate device characterization.
